plan.topic: What does BSL-3 actually mean? The containment layers that keep plague inside a lab
plan.angle: Plague Labs: What Does BSL-3 Actually Mean? One idea: BSL-3 is a set of containment layers. Air flows inward and is exhausted through HEPA filters, work happens inside biosafety cabinets, staff wear respirators and PPE, entry is controlled and incidents are reported straight away. Under CDC/NIH BMBL, plague work moves up to BSL-3 when it can create aerosols or involves large quantities, and most clinical-sample work uses BSL-2 practices. After a possible exposure: medical review, monitoring, and preventive antibiotics only if clinicians decide they're needed. Hedge line: 'Irkutsk oblast: plague suspected in media reports, not officially confirmed. WHO says the cause of death is not yet known (as of Oct 8, 2026).' Don't apply the BSL scheme to the Russian lab, and no leak speculation. Point to the full video. Close with 'If you're worried, talk to a health professional.'

plan.why: Spin-off of L1, which drives traffic to the long video. It's an emerging question with low competition and a concrete subject plus a plain-question title. | fact-check: The same scope problem as L1. The working framing ('containment layers that keep plague inside a lab', with BSL-3 implied as the plague standard) misstates BMBL. BMBL recommends BSL-2 for most Y. pestis clinical and culture work, and BSL-3 for aerosol-prone or large-scale work. The hedge line is fine, but date it to the WHO statement (Oct 6–8) and say 'not officially confirmed'. Don't tie the BSL layers to the Irkutsk institute (Russia uses its own classification). Keep it to about 60 s and 170 words or fewer.

package.description:
As of Oct 7, 2026, Russian authorities told WHO there's no evidence pneumonic plague played a part in the Irkutsk oblast lab worker's death (UN News); WHO said no cause of death had been officially confirmed as of Oct 6. Under the US CDC/NIH biosafety manual (not a description of that lab), clinical plague samples start at BSL-2; BSL-3 is recommended for aerosol-prone work or large, concentrated amounts, and it's layers: inward airflow, biosafety cabinets, protective gear, controlled entry. Possible exposure or symptoms like fever, cough, shortness of breath or chest pain? Contact a doctor or local health authority urgently.

Next come two dated status hedges, each credited to the body that said it. WHO, as of Oct 6: no cause of death officially confirmed. Russian authorities to WHO, as of Oct 7: no evidence pneumonic plague played a part. Then the scope line: 'this is the US system, not that lab'. The answer arrives by about second 30: under BMBL, clinical samples start at BSL-2, and BSL-3 is for aerosol-prone or concentrated work. After that, a numbered layer countdown, an urgent-care line, and a loop back to the hook ('BSL-3 isn't one wall. It's layers.').

factcheck.summary:
The science part of this Short is accurate. It matches BMBL: clinical plague samples and cultures at BSL-2, BSL-3 for aerosol-prone or concentrated work, and the descriptions of inward airflow, non-recirculated exhaust, HEPA filtration per the risk assessment, biosafety cabinets, PPE, controlled entry and incident reporting are all consistent. The CDC's warning signs and the urgent-care line are in place. All 5 sources exist and their URLs work.

The fixes needed are all in the status block:
1. **s3 on-screen text is stronger than the source.** It says "no evidence of plague". Russia's actual words, quoted by WHO's Tedros, were "no evidence pneumonic plague played a part".
2. **s3 drops the open question.** It omits that WHO asked for more information on Oct 7 (UN News), so it reads as if the case is closed.
3. **The contacts line has the wrong date.** "No dangerous pathogens among her contacts" comes from the Oct 6 UN News report. The Oct 7 article only says "no pathogens had been detected".
4. **The status is out of date.** On Oct 8, WHO's Tedros asked Russia to clarify media reports of a second employee with pneumonia of undetermined cause (Al Jazeera, CNN). Russia's health regulator said no infections were found among staff.

The script runs about 220 words (~85–90 s). That's under the 178 s limit, but over the 170-word guide.

issues.claim: Russia to WHO: no evidence of plague (as of Oct 7)
issues.problem: This is stronger than what the source says. Russia told WHO there was 'no evidence pneumonic plague played a part in her death' (UN News, Oct 7). That is not the same as no evidence of plague, and not confirmed ≠ ruled out. The text is also stronger than the narration.
issues.fix: Russia to WHO: no evidence pneumonic plague played a part (Oct 7)

issues.claim: As of October 7, Russian authorities told WHO there was no evidence pneumonic plague played a part in her death, and no dangerous pathogens were detected among her contacts.
issues.problem: Two problems. (1) The line about no dangerous pathogens among contacts comes from the Oct 6 UN News report. The Oct 7 article says only 'no pathogens had been detected'. (2) The narration leaves out that WHO asked for more information and lab results on Oct 7, so the status sounds settled when WHO is still assessing.
issues.fix: As of October 7, Russian authorities told WHO there was no evidence pneumonic plague played a part in her death, and no pathogens had been detected. WHO has asked for more information and lab results. What follows is the US system, not a description of that lab.

issues.claim: The status is complete as of Oct 7
issues.problem: The status has changed since. On Oct 8, WHO Director-General Tedros asked Russia to clarify 'media reports of a second employee with pneumonia of undetermined cause'. Russia's regulator said no infections were detected among staff, and the Kremlin called most media reports false (Al Jazeera, Oct 8; CNN). Viewers will see this news, so leaving it out makes the Short look out of date.
issues.fix: Add a sentence after the WHO line in s3: "On October 8, WHO asked Russia to clarify media reports of a second staff member with pneumonia. Russia's health regulator said no infections were found among staff." Before publishing, re-check WHO, UN News and Rospotrebnadzor, and re-date the lines.

issues.claim: Plague was suspected in media reports.
issues.problem: This undersells what WHO said. WHO's spokesperson said authorities were investigating 'whether pneumonic plague caused her death'. That is an official line, not only media reports.
issues.fix: Status: a lab worker in Irkutsk oblast died of severe pneumonia. As of October 6, 2026, WHO said no cause of death had been officially confirmed, and authorities were investigating whether pneumonic plague caused it.

issues.claim: After a lab exposure: medical review, monitoring, and preventive antibiotics when clinicians decide they're needed.
issues.problem: The cited CDC clinical-care page supports post-exposure prophylaxis for 'persons with known exposure', but it doesn't mention monitoring. The evaluation and reporting of exposure incidents comes from BMBL.
issues.fix: Add 'bmbl' to the s7 source_ids. Optionally reword to: "After a possible lab exposure: it's evaluated right away, and clinicians decide on preventive antibiotics."

issues.claim: Four: controlled entry, incidents reported immediately.
issues.problem: BMBL says incidents must be evaluated immediately and reported. The current wording is close but slightly compresses this.
issues.fix: Four: controlled entry, and any incident evaluated and reported right away.

issues.problem: This is over the 170-word guide for Shorts (about 85–90 s). It's under the 178 s limit, but our notes say shorter performs better, and the s3 additions add more words.
issues.fix: Cut the s6 pivot 'The last two are about people.' and shorten s8 to: "If you're worried, talk to a health professional. BSL-3 isn't one wall. It's layers." Keep the long-video CTA in the caption only.

hold_reason: Dropped by Editor-in-Chief: The BSL-3 science is accurate, but the fact-checker's major status problems are still in the video. The s3 on-screen text says "no evidence of plague", which is stronger than the source's "no evidence pneumonic plague played a part". The video also leaves out that WHO is still asking for information and doesn't mention the Oct 8 report of a second staff member, so viewers would think the case is settled. Rewrite and re-date s3 against current WHO, UN News and Rospotrebnadzor statements, move the contacts line to Oct 6 (Instagram caption too), then republish.

notes: The 'Pneumonia' label next to the lungs icon is tiny (well under the 40px rule) and low-contrast red-on-pink — unreadable at a glance.
Caption reads 'BUT AS OF OCTOBER SIXTH,' — the date is spelled out in words instead of numerals, breaking the caption-numerals rule and risking a mis-sync with the on-screen headline.

Critical: the caption on this shot reads 'HAD BEEN OFFICIALLY CONFIRMED.' with no 'NOT' — it directly contradicts the on-screen headline 'Not confirmed / WHO, as of Oct 6, 2026' and flips the accuracy-critical status claim. This is the same recurring bug flagged in prior QA (status word split from its negation).
Caption 'TWENTY TWENTY-SIX,' spells out the year instead of using the numeral '2026'.
Caption 'THEN, AS OF OCTOBER SEVENTH,' spells the date out instead of using numerals ('Oct 7').

Caption 'EVIDENCE PNEUMONIC PLAGUE' is truncated — it appears to drop the leading 'No' from 'No evidence of pneumonic plague,' so on its own it reads as confirming plague evidence, the opposite of the headline's meaning.
Caption splits the term 'BSL-2' awkwardly across two lines as 'AT BSL-' / '2 PRACTICES', breaking the number off its label.

audio.soundNotes: Music sits at -13.5 dB under voice and -13.3 in pauses, already inside the target window, so kept gain at 1.0 and left pauses alone. Thinned redundant duplicate-timestamp SFX (tick/whip/whoosh doubled on the same pop/swoosh) at the busiest reveal moments (t≈12, 27.6, 36.5, 40.2, 45.8, 52.6, 57.5, 60, 64, 67.7, 71.3, 75, 83.9, 89.5, 93.1, 99.4) so no beat carries more than 3-4 audible effects, and pulled down a handful of cues that measured too hot during speech (t≈5.9, 29.5, 32.4, 41.3, 58.5) into the -14 to -20 dB felt range. Softened the hit/swoosh under the serious "Contact a doctor urgently" line so the warning lands cleanly, and added five bespoke, understated lab-ambience and resolve cues (HVAC hum, air hiss, cabinet fan, a single calm heartbeat pulse, and a warm closing chime) to reinforce key beats without competing with narration.
